QuestionText: Which of the following is prepared first while preparing the final accounts of a sole proprietorship
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Trading Account is prepared first to determine the Gross Profit or Gross Loss, which is then transferred to the Profit and Loss Account.

QuestionText: Gross Profit is calculated by deducting which of the following from Net Sales
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Gross Profit equals Net Sales minus Cost of Goods Sold. It represents profit before deducting operating expenses.

QuestionText: Outstanding expenses at the end of the year are shown in the Balance Sheet as:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Outstanding expenses represent amounts owed but not yet paid, hence they are shown as current liabilities in the Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Prepaid insurance appearing in the Trial Balance should be shown in:
Options: B) Profit and Loss Account - Credit side
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Prepaid expenses represent benefits yet to be received, hence they are treated as current assets in the Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Which of the following items appears on the credit side of the Trading Account
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Closing Stock appears on the credit side of the Trading Account and as an asset in the Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Depreciation on machinery is debited to:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Depreciation is debited to Profit and Loss Account as an expense and credited to Machinery Account to reduce its book value.

QuestionText: If Opening Stock is Rs. 20,000, Purchases Rs. 80,000, and Closing Stock is Rs. 15,000, what is the Cost of Goods Sold
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock = Rs. 20,000 + Rs. 80,000 - Rs. 15,000 = Rs. 85,000.

QuestionText: Goods withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use should be:
Options: C) Debited to Drawings Account and Credited to Purchases Account
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: When goods are taken for personal use, Drawings Account is debited and Purchases Account is credited to reduce the cost of goods available for sale.

QuestionText: Accrued income is shown in the Balance Sheet as:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Accrued income represents income earned but not yet received, hence it is shown as a current asset in the Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Income received in advance is treated as:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Income received in advance represents an obligation to provide goods or services in the future, hence it is a current liability.

QuestionText: Which method of maintaining accounts does not follow the double entry system completely
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Single Entry System does not follow the double entry system completely as only personal accounts or cash book may be maintained.

QuestionText: Under the Statement of Affairs method, profit is calculated as:
Options: A) Closing Capital + Drawings - Additional Capital - Opening Capital
B) Opening Capital + Additional Capital - Drawings - Closing Capital
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Profit = Closing Capital + Drawings - Additional Capital - Opening Capital. This formula adjusts for capital movements during the year.

QuestionText: The Statement of Affairs is similar to:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Statement of Affairs is similar to a Balance Sheet as it shows assets and liabilities, but it is prepared from incomplete records.

QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT shown in the Trading Account
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Salaries is an indirect expense shown in the Profit and Loss Account, not in the Trading Account.

QuestionText: Provision for doubtful debts is created against:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Provision for doubtful debts is created on debtors to account for the estimated amount that may not be recovered.

QuestionText: If Sales are Rs. 5,00,000 and Gross Profit is 20% on sales, what is the Cost of Goods Sold
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Gross Profit = 20% of Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000. Cost of Goods Sold = Sales - Gross Profit = Rs. 5,00,000 - Rs. 1,00,000 = Rs. 4,00,000.

QuestionText: Carriage outward is shown in:
Options: C) Profit and Loss Account - Debit side
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Carriage outward is a selling expense incurred on goods sold, hence it appears on the debit side of the Profit and Loss Account.

QuestionText: Opening Capital can be calculated as:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Opening Capital = Opening Assets - Opening Liabilities. This is based on the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a direct expense
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Factory lighting is a direct expense related to manufacturing and is shown in the Trading Account.

QuestionText: The excess of credit side over debit side of Trading Account represents:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: When the credit side (Sales + Closing Stock) exceeds the debit side (Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses), it indicates Gross Profit.

QuestionText: Ram started business with Rs. 50,000. At the end of the year, his capital was Rs. 65,000. He withdrew Rs. 10,000 during the year. What is the profit earned
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Profit = Closing Capital + Drawings - Opening Capital = Rs. 65,000 + Rs. 10,000 - Rs. 50,000 = Rs. 25,000.

QuestionText: Bad debts recovered, if appearing in Trial Balance, is shown in:
Options: B) Profit and Loss Account - Credit side
D) Profit and Loss Account - Debit side
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Bad debts recovered is an income and hence shown on the credit side of the Profit and Loss Account.

QuestionText: Closing stock is valued at:
Options: C) Cost or market price, whichever is lower
D) Cost or market price, whichever is higher
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: As per the principle of conservatism, closing stock is valued at cost or market price, whichever is lower.

QuestionText: Which account is closed by transferring its balance to Capital Account
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: The balance of Profit and Loss Account (Net Profit or Net Loss) is transferred to the Capital Account of the proprietor.

QuestionText: A machine costing Rs. 1,00,000 is depreciated at 10% p.a. on straight line method. What is the depreciation for the first year
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Under Straight Line Method, Depreciation = Cost x Rate = Rs. 1,00,000 x 10% = Rs. 10,000 per year.

QuestionText: If rent paid during the year is Rs. 24,000 and rent outstanding at year end is Rs. 2,000, the rent expense to be shown in Profit and Loss Account is:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Rent expense = Rent Paid + Outstanding Rent = Rs. 24,000 + Rs. 2,000 = Rs. 26,000.

QuestionText: Debtors in the Trial Balance are Rs. 50,000. Additional information: Bad debts to be written off Rs. 2,000, Provision for bad debts to be maintained at 5%. What is the net amount of debtors in Balance Sheet
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Debtors after bad debts = Rs. 50,000 - Rs. 2,000 = Rs. 48,000. Provision = 5% of Rs. 48,000 = Rs. 2,400. Net Debtors = Rs. 48,000 - Rs. 2,400 = Rs. 45,600.

QuestionText: In the conversion method of incomplete records, which account is prepared to find the credit purchases
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Total Creditors Account is prepared to ascertain the credit purchases when complete records are not available.

QuestionText: Which of the following items will increase the Capital of a sole proprietor
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Additional capital introduced by the proprietor increases the capital, while drawings and net loss decrease it.

QuestionText: Wages paid for installation of new machinery should be:
Options: C) Debited to Profit and Loss Account
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Wages paid for installation of machinery is a capital expenditure and should be added to the cost of machinery.

QuestionText: Sales as per Trading Account is Rs. 3,00,000. If Sales Returns are Rs. 15,000, what is the Gross Sales
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Net Sales = Gross Sales - Sales Returns. So, Gross Sales = Net Sales + Sales Returns = Rs. 3,00,000 + Rs. 15,000 = Rs. 3,15,000.

QuestionText: A trader maintains books under single entry system. His assets on 1st April 2023 were Rs. 2,50,000 and liabilities Rs. 80,000. On 31st March 2024, assets were Rs. 3,20,000 and liabilities Rs. 1,00,000. During the year he introduced Rs. 30,000 and withdrew Rs. 40,000. Calculate the profit or loss for the year.
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship

QuestionText: Insurance premium paid Rs. 12,000 for the year ending 30th June 2024. If the accounting year ends on 31st March 2024, the prepaid insurance is:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Insurance for 3 months (April to June 2024) is prepaid. Prepaid Insurance = Rs. 12,000 x 3/12 = Rs. 3,000.

QuestionText: Commission received in advance is:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Commission received in advance is unearned revenue and represents an obligation, hence it is a current liability.

QuestionText: Which of the following errors will affect the Trial Balance
Options: D) Wrong totaling of Purchase Book
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Wrong totaling of Purchase Book will cause unequal debits and credits, affecting the Trial Balance agreement.

QuestionText: Goods costing Rs. 5,000 given as charity should be credited to:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Goods given as charity are credited to Purchases Account (to reduce purchases) and debited to Charity Account (as expense).

QuestionText: Under reducing balance method, a machine costing Rs. 80,000 is depreciated at 10% p.a. What is the book value at the end of second year
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Year 1 Depreciation = Rs. 80,000 x 10% = Rs. 8,000; Book Value = Rs. 72,000. Year 2 Depreciation = Rs. 72,000 x 10% = Rs. 7,200; Book Value = Rs. 64,800.

QuestionText: Which of the following appears on both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Closing Stock appears on the credit side of Trading Account and as a current asset in the Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Interest on capital is:
Options: A) An expense for the business and income for proprietor
B) An income for the business
C) A loss for the proprietor
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Interest on capital is debited to Profit and Loss Account (expense) and credited to Capital Account (income for proprietor).

QuestionText: Total Debtors Account is prepared to ascertain:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Total Debtors Account is prepared under the conversion method to find out credit sales from incomplete records.

QuestionText: Debtors at the beginning Rs. 40,000; at the end Rs. 50,000; Cash received from debtors Rs. 2,00,000; Bad debts Rs. 5,000; Sales Returns Rs. 3,000. Credit Sales for the year are:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Credit Sales = Closing Debtors + Cash Received + Bad Debts + Returns - Opening Debtors = Rs. 50,000 + Rs. 2,00,000 + Rs. 5,000 + Rs. 3,000 - Rs. 40,000 = Rs. 2,18,000.

QuestionText: Reserve for discount on debtors is shown as:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Reserve for discount on debtors is created for expected discount to be allowed and is shown as deduction from debtors in Balance Sheet.

QuestionText: Goods sent on approval basis and not yet approved by customer at year end should be:
Options: B) Excluded from sales and included in closing stock
D) Written off as bad debt
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Goods on approval not yet approved are not sales; they should be removed from sales and included in closing stock at cost.

QuestionText: The balance sheet shows:
Options: A) Financial position on a particular date
B) Financial performance over a period
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Balance Sheet is a statement showing financial position of a business on a particular date by listing assets, liabilities and capital.

QuestionText: Goods destroyed by fire Rs. 10,000 (insured for Rs. 8,000). The treatment in final accounts will be:
Options: A) Credit Trading Account Rs. 10,000, Debit Insurance Claim Rs. 8,000, Debit P&L Rs. 2,000
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Goods destroyed are credited to Trading Account at cost, insurance claim is shown as asset, and uninsured loss is debited to P&L Account.

QuestionText: If Gross Profit is 25% on cost and Sales are Rs. 2,50,000, what is the Gross Profit
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: If GP is 25% on cost, then GP is 25/125 = 20% on sales. GP = Rs. 2,50,000 x 20% = Rs. 50,000.

QuestionText: Creditors at beginning Rs. 30,000; at end Rs. 45,000; Cash paid to creditors Rs. 1,80,000; Discount received Rs. 3,000; Purchase Returns Rs. 2,000. Credit Purchases are:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Credit Purchases = Closing Creditors + Cash Paid + Discount + Returns - Opening Creditors = Rs. 45,000 + Rs. 1,80,000 + Rs. 3,000 + Rs. 2,000 - Rs. 30,000 = Rs. 2,00,000.

QuestionText: Discount column on the debit side of Cash Book represents:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Discount column on debit side records discount allowed to customers when they make payments.

QuestionText: Mohan's capital on 1st April 2023 was Rs. 1,00,000. He introduced additional capital of Rs. 20,000 on 1st October 2023. Interest on capital is allowed at 6% p.a. Interest on capital for the year is:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship

QuestionText: Manager is entitled to commission of 10% on net profit after charging such commission. If net profit before commission is Rs. 55,000, the commission is:
Topic: Commerce - Financial Statements of Sole Proprietorship
Explanation: Commission = 10/110 x Rs. 55,000 = Rs. 5,000. Net Profit after commission = Rs. 55,000 - Rs. 5,000 = Rs. 50,000.
